title: The check loss elicits the quantile
title_html: The check loss elicits the quantile
html:
Let Y be a random variable with distribution function F and E|Y|<∞, and let G(q)=Eρτ(Y−q).

  1. Population characterization. G is finite and convex, and for q<q′ G(q′)−G(q)=∫qq′{F(s)−τ}ds.{#eq-qnt-difference}

    Consequently the set of minimizers of G is exactly the set of τ-quantiles of F, that is {q:F(q−)≤τ≤F(q)}.

  2. Linear program. Writing ui=(yi−x(i)⊤b)+ and vi=(x(i)⊤b−yi)+, problem @eq-qnt-sample is equivalent to minb,u,v{τ1⊤u+(1−τ)1⊤v}subject toXb+u−v=y,  u≥0, v≥0,{#eq-qnt-lp}

    a linear program in 2n+2p nonnegative variables with n equality constraints.

  3. Equivariance of the estimate. Let 𝛃β^τ(y,X) denote any solution of @eq-qnt-sample. For a>0, 𝛄γ∈Rp and nonsingular A, 𝛃𝛃𝛃𝛃𝛃𝛄𝛃𝛄𝛃𝛃β^τ(ay,X)=aβ^τ(y,X),β^τ(−y,X)=−β^1−τ(y,X),β^τ(y+Xγ,X)=β^τ(y,X)+γ,β^τ(y,XA)=A−1β^τ(y,X).

  4. Equivariance under monotone maps. For strictly increasing left-continuous h, Qh(Y)(τ∣x)=h{QY(τ∣x)}.
